reviewers.summary: The manuscript reports a propensity score matching analysis but contains major deficiencies: an unclear research question, mischaracterization of the method, a high unmatched treated rate and poor covariate balance not discussed, missing diagnostic details, and an overinterpreted conclusion. These issues make the results unreliable and the manuscript not ready for dissemination.

findings.title: Unclear research question
findings.whyItMatters: The study repeatedly refers to a 'prespecified study question' but never states it. Without a clear PICO/PECOT, the analysis cannot be evaluated for appropriateness or bias.
findings.actionableFix: Explicitly state the research question, including target population, exposure (treatment), comparator (control), outcome (outcome_binary), and time horizon if relevant.

findings.title: Method mischaracterization
findings.whyItMatters: The manuscript describes the analysis as a 'logistic model', but the actual method is nearest-neighbor propensity score matching. This inconsistency misleads readers and undermines the validity of the report.
findings.actionableFix: Correct the methods section to accurately describe the propensity score modeling, matching algorithm, caliper, exact matching on sex, and estimand (ATT).

findings.title: High proportion of unmatched treated subjects (53%) not disclosed
findings.whyItMatters: Loss of 53% of treated subjects likely introduces selection bias and limits generalizability to the subgroup that could be matched. The manuscript does not mention this critical limitation.
findings.actionableFix: Report the number and proportion of unmatched treated, compare their baseline characteristics to matched subjects, discuss potential bias, and consider relaxing caliper or using alternative methods.

findings.title: Post-matching covariate imbalance not reported or addressed
findings.whyItMatters: Residual standardized mean differences up to 0.233 indicate that confounding remains, biasing the effect estimate. The manuscript omits all balance assessment.
findings.actionableFix: Present pre- and post-matching balance (e.g., love plot or table of SMDs), discuss whether residual imbalance is acceptable, and consider additional modeling or matching refinement.

findings.title: Missing essential methods detail
findings.whyItMatters: The manuscript lacks a description of the propensity model, variables included (age, severity, albumin), exact matching on sex, caliper width, matching ratio, and model diagnostics. This makes it impossible for readers to assess validity.
findings.actionableFix: Provide a complete methods section describing all analytical choices, including how the propensity score was estimated, matching specifications, and how balance was evaluated.

findings.title: Overly precise p-value and missing confidence interval
findings.whyItMatters: Reporting p=1.0000 is unnecessarily precise and may be a rounding artifact. The odds ratio is given without its confidence interval, obscuring the precision of the estimate.
findings.actionableFix: Report p > 0.99, and always present the 95% CI (0.48, 2.08) alongside the OR. Also include the risk difference and group sample sizes.

findings.title: Limitations section is generic and ignores actual problems
findings.whyItMatters: The limitations mention missingness and complete-case analysis (non-issues here) but fail to address the large proportion of unmatched subjects, residual confounding, and absence of sensitivity analyses. This misguides readers.
findings.actionableFix: Revise the limitations to focus on the specific threats identified in the analysis: selection from unmatched treated, imbalance, unmeasured confounding, and limited sample size.

findings.title: No sensitivity analysis for unmeasured confounding
findings.whyItMatters: Propensity score matching only adjusts for measured covariates. Without a quantitative bias analysis (e.g., E-value), the claim of 'interpretable' may overstate certainty.
findings.actionableFix: Either perform a sensitivity analysis (Rosenbaum bounds or E-value) or explicitly downgrade the conclusion to 'unadjusted for unmeasured confounders'.

missingEvidence: Specification of the prespecified research question (PECOT)
Detailed balance tables (pre- and post-matching) and love plot
Characteristics of matched versus unmatched treated subjects
Propensity model coefficients and model fit diagnostics (AUC, calibration)
Sensitivity analysis for unobserved confounding (e.g., E-value)

reviewers.summary: The manuscript is an autogenerated placeholder lacking essential details about the study question, exposure, outcome, cohort, matching procedure, and diagnostics. Propensity score matching failed to achieve balance (post-matching SMD >0.1 for all covariates) and discarded 53% of treated individuals, yet the manuscript does not report or interpret these critical flaws. The reported OR=1.0 with wide CI is uninformative and presented without appropriate caveats. The manuscript cannot be published in its current form and requires a complete rewrite with honest reporting of the failed analysis.

findings.title: Manuscript is an autogenerated template, not a scientific report
findings.whyItMatters: The manuscript lacks a defined study question, exposure/outcome definitions, variable descriptions, cohort eligibility, matching details, balance diagnostics, and any meaningful discussion. Placeholder text (e.g., 'No reader-facing paper/manuscript artifact was found') and a generic limitations list make it unsuitable for any audience.
findings.actionableFix: Write a proper manuscript that specifies the research question, describes the data and methods in detail, presents all relevant diagnostics (balance, overlap, matched vs. unmatched characteristics), and interprets results in the context of the methodological shortcomings.

findings.title: Post-matching covariate balance is inadequate
findings.whyItMatters: After matching, all three continuous covariates (age, severity, albumin) still have absolute standardized mean differences >0.1 (max 0.233), indicating residual imbalance that may bias the estimated treatment effect. The manuscript neither reports these SMDs nor acknowledges the failure to achieve balance.
findings.actionableFix: Report the balance statistics (e.g., in a table) and either (a) repeat the analysis with a tighter caliper, additional covariates, or alternative matching methods to improve balance, or (b) clearly state that the matching failed and interpret the results as unreliable due to residual confounding.

findings.title: 53% of treated individuals excluded from analysis without characterization
findings.whyItMatters: 77 out of 144 treated subjects (53%) were unmatched, changing the effective population for the ATT estimate. The manuscript does not discuss the characteristics of excluded treated or how the estimated effect applies only to the matched subset, thus misleading readers about generalizability.
findings.actionableFix: Describe the matched vs. unmatched treated groups (demographics, outcomes, propensity score distribution). If the unmatched group differs substantially, report the limitation and consider sensitivity analyses (e.g., weighting for the unmatched).

findings.title: Essential propensity score diagnostics not presented
findings.whyItMatters: Standard PS matching reporting includes a balance table, love plot, propensity score overlap graph, and discussion of common support. None are provided, despite the artifacts containing the raw data (e.g., balance.csv, propensity-overlap.csv). This prevents readers from evaluating the matching quality.
findings.actionableFix: Include all standard diagnostics (balance table with SMDs, a love plot, a histogram or mirror histogram of propensity scores by treatment group, and a discussion of common support). Also note the figure-qa warning and ensure all diagnostic plots are generated.

findings.title: Interpretation as 'interpretable local evidence' is unsafe
findings.whyItMatters: Given the failed balance and large unmatched fraction, the point estimate (OR=1.0) and its wide CI (0.48–2.08) cannot be interpreted as evidence of no effect or as a reliable local estimate. The conclusion overstates the certainty and risks misinterpretation.
findings.actionableFix: Revise the discussion to emphasize that the matching did not achieve balance, that the estimate is likely biased, and that no conclusion about treatment effect can be drawn. Avoid any language that implies the analysis provides interpretable evidence.

findings.title: No data provenance or variable definitions provided
findings.whyItMatters: Without information on data source, collection methods, and variable coding (e.g., how severity and albumin were measured), the plausibility and external validity of the dataset cannot be assessed. This is a reproducibility requirement.
findings.actionableFix: Add a Data Source section describing the origin of the dataset, variable definitions, and any relevant quality checks. For variables like severity, provide the scale or reference.

findings.title: Diagnostic figures missing despite figure-qa warning
findings.whyItMatters: The stats-run artifact reports a figure-qa warning with 0/0 figures passed, indicating no diagnostic plots were produced. Visual diagnostics (propensity score overlap, balance plots) are critical for evaluating PS matching.
findings.actionableFix: Generate and include the standard diagnostic figures. Ensure figure-qa passes by including at least a love plot and a propensity score distribution plot.

findings.title: Limitations section is generic and not analysis-specific
findings.whyItMatters: The limitations list includes irrelevant points (e.g., 'Logistic-type model detected; explicit separation diagnostic evidence was not found') and fails to mention the specific flaws of this analysis: residual imbalance and unmatched treated. This suggests a placeholder text was not reviewed.
findings.actionableFix: Replace the generic limitations with a tailored description of the actual limitations: poor balance, loss of treated subjects, no sensitivity analysis, single dataset, and the impossibility of drawing causal inferences.

missingEvidence: Data source description and variable definitions
Cohort selection criteria and eligibility rules
Propensity score distribution plot or overlap plot
Characteristics of matched vs. unmatched treated subjects
Interpretation of results in the context of failed matching

reviewPanel.nextAction: Adjudicate findings and route accepted repairs back into the pipeline.
